THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

Respondent Nos.2 to 5 had filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C alleging that without the knowledge or consent of legal representatives of the late Basappa or successors of Late Mallanna and also the complainant herein, the accused No.1 without having any independent right title conveyed the subject land in favour of accused No.2 by executing the registered gift deed dated 10.04.2014 which was standing in the name of Mallanna s/o Basappa taking advantage of similarity in the name of Mallanna s/o Basappa.

It was further alleged that, the accused No.1 was fully aware that the complainant and other legal representatives of Mallanna s/o Basappa have executed an agreement of consent dated 14.08.2009 stating that possession to an extent of 10 guntas in the subject land has been delivered for construction of Mahadeshwara Temple.
2. The learned Magistrate referred the complaint to the police for investigation under Section 156(3).

The police after investigation submitted the charge sheet for the offence under Sections 120,
419, 420, 468, 471, 504 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the allegations that accused No.1 without authority of law has executed the gift deed in favour of the accused No.2 does not constitute an offence either for cheating or forgery as specified under the provisions of IPC.

4. On the other hand, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent-State submits that accused No.2 clandestinely the executed the gift deed in favour of the accused No.2 though he had no absolute right over the subject land with an intention to cheat the complainant and other family members.

He further submits that the allegations made in the complaint clearly discloses that accused No.1 by executing the gift deed in favour of accused No.2 has committed the offence of forgery and cheating and the learned Magistrate has rightly taken cognizance.
5. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.
6. To constitute an offence of cheating as specified under Section 415 of IPC, a person must have dishonestly induces the other person so deceived to deliver any property to any person.
In other words, the person must have induced the other person to deliver any property with an intention to cheat.
In the instant case, there is no allegations that accused No.2 induced the C.W.5 to deliver any property to accused No.1 with an intention to cheat.
In the absence of essential ingredients, so as to constitute the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is impermissible.

7. To constitute the commission of offence of forgery as specified under Sections 463 and 464 of IPC Sri Mallaiah vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49160755/

sentences.text: (b) A, without Z 's authority, affixes Z 's seal to a document purporting to be a conveyance of an estate from Z to A, with the intention of selling the estate to B, and thereby of obtaining from B the purchase-money.
A has committed forgery.

8. In the instant case, there is no material that accused No.1 has forged the signature of husband of C.W.5 and conveyed the subject land in favour of accused No.2 stating that the property belongs to husband of C.W.5.

The gift deed specifies that the subject land is the ancestral property inherited by him, and has the authority to execute the gift deed which does not satisfy the essential ingredients so as to constitute the commission of offence of forgery as specified under Sections 463 and 464 of IPC.
Hence, in the absence of essential ingredients, the cognizance taken for the offence of forgery is also impermissible.

9. Even accepting the allegations made in the private complaint on the face of it, utmost,
tantamounts execution of gift deed by accused No.1 in favour of accused No.2 without having absolute right.
In view of preceding analysis, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1165/2016 on the file of Prinicpal/Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Nelamangala is hereby quashed.
